findings.summary: The break-even point for prompt caching is stated one request too late.
findings.evidence: "Reuses a prefix of the prompt; pays off from the second hit"
findings.fix: Write: "pays off after the first hit (1.25× write + 0.1× read ≈ 1.35× vs 2× uncached over two requests)".

findings.summary: The break-even point for caching is stated ambiguously. With the listed prices, the cache already pays off on the first read.
findings.evidence: "pays off from the second hit" (write 1.25× + one read 0.1× = 1.35×, against 2× uncached for two requests)
findings.fix: Say "pays off from the first cache read (the second request)".

findings.summary: One bullet holds two ideas: total time is unchanged, and TTFT drops.
findings.evidence: "Total time is the same; TTFT drops, so the UI feels fast"
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: "Total time unchanged" and "TTFT drops, so the UI feels fast".

findings.summary: The OpenTelemetry code block comes before any line stating the idea it shows. The explanation is a caption placed after the code.
findings.evidence: "2. Viewing and Slicing" opens directly with the python block, and the caption "OpenTelemetry span with slicing metadata" follows it.
findings.fix: Put a one-line idea first, e.g. "Attach slicing metadata as span attributes", then show the code.

findings.summary: The cache-friendly prompt order uses different names for the same layers than page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 2: "Stable docs", "Conversation", "New user turn". Page 6: "Stable context", "History", "New turn".
findings.fix: Use one set of names on both pages, e.g. Tools, System, Stable docs, History, New turn.
